paper_title: Rethinking Robust Adaptation: Characterization of Structural Mechanisms for Biochemical Network Robustness through Topological Invariants (Hirono, 2025, PRX Life)
core_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
If \(\gamma=(V_\gamma,E_\gamma)\) is output-complete and \(\lambda(\gamma)=0\), then every species and reaction outside \(\gamma\) has robust perfect adaptation with respect to every reaction-parameter perturbation inside \(\gamma\):
\[
e_B\in E_\gamma,
\quad v_i\in V\setminus V_\gamma,
\quad e_A\in E\setminus E_\gamma
\Longrightarrow
\partial_B\bar x_i=0\text{ and }\partial_B\bar r_A=0.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1)& \gamma=(V_\gamma,E_\gamma)\text{ is output-complete}.\\
(P2)& \lambda(\gamma):=-|V_\gamma|+|E_\gamma|-|(\ker S)_{\mathrm{supp}\,\gamma}|+|P^0_\gamma(\operatorname{coker}S)|.\\
(P3)& \lambda(\gamma)=0.\\
(P4)& \text{Law of localization: if (P1) and (P3) hold, then }\\
&\partial_B\bar x_i=0\text{ and }\partial_B\bar r_A=0\text{ for all }e_B\in E_\gamma,\ v_i\notin V_\gamma,\ e_A\notin E_\gamma.\\
(P5)& \text{RPA with respect to }k_B\text{ means }\partial_B\bar x_i=0\text{ or }\partial_B\bar r_A=0\text{ at steady state.}
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Let \(e_B\in E_\gamma\), \(v_i\in V\setminus V_\gamma\), and \(e_A\in E\setminus E_\gamma\). Then
\begin{align}
\lambda(\gamma)
&=0 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
\gamma\text{ is output-complete}
& &&\text{by (P1)}\\
\partial_B\bar x_i
&=0 &&\text{by (P4)}\\
\partial_B\bar r_A
&=0 &&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}
Using the definition of RPA,
\begin{align}
\partial_B\bar x_i=0
&\Longrightarrow \bar x_i\text{ has RPA with respect to }k_B &&\text{by (P5)},\\
\partial_B\bar r_A=0
&\Longrightarrow \bar r_A\text{ has RPA with respect to }k_B &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{e_B\in E_\gamma,\ v_i\notin V_\gamma,\ e_A\notin E_\gamma
\Longrightarrow
\partial_B\bar x_i=0\text{ and }\partial_B\bar r_A=0}
\]

\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\section*{Claim}
Let \(e_B\) be a perturbed reaction. Define the affected sets
\[
V_B:=\{v_i\in V:\partial_B\bar x_i\ne0\},
\qquad
E_B:=\{e_A\in E:\partial_B\bar r_A\ne0\},
\]
and the output-completion set
\[
E_B^+:=\{e_C\in E\setminus E_B:\operatorname{React}(e_C)\cap V_B\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
Then \(\gamma_B:=(V_B,E_B\cup E_B^+)\) is output-complete, and the influence of any reaction in \(E_B\cup E_B^+\) is localized inside \(\gamma_B\).

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1)& V_B:=\{v_i\in V:\partial_B\bar x_i\ne0\}.\\
(P2)& E_B:=\{e_A\in E:\partial_B\bar r_A\ne0\}.\\
(P3)& E_B^+:=\{e_C\in E\setminus E_B:\operatorname{React}(e_C)\cap V_B\ne\varnothing\}.\\
(P4)& \gamma_B:=(V_B,E_B\cup E_B^+).\\
(P5)& \text{Output-complete means: if }v_i\in V_\gamma\text{ and }v_i\in\operatorname{React}(e_C),\text{ then }e_C\in E_\gamma.\\
(P6)& \text{Transitivity: }e_A\rightsquigarrow v_i,\ v_i\in\operatorname{React}(e_C),\ e_C\rightsquigarrow e_D\Longrightarrow e_A\rightsquigarrow e_D.\\
(P7)& \text{If }e_C\in E_B^+\text{ and }v_i\in\operatorname{React}(e_C)\cap V_B,\text{ then }e_B\rightsquigarrow v_i.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
First prove output-completeness. Let \(v_i\in V_B\) and \(v_i\in\operatorname{React}(e_C)\). Then
\begin{align}
e_C\in E_B
&\Longrightarrow e_C\in E_B\cup E_B^+ &&\text{set inclusion},\\
e_C\notin E_B
&\Longrightarrow e_C\in E_B^+ &&\text{by (P3), since }v_i\in V_B\cap\operatorname{React}(e_C),\\
e_C\in E_B\cup E_B^+
& &&\text{in either case}.
\end{align}
Thus \(\gamma_B\) is output-complete by (P5).
Now let \(e_C\in E_B^+\) and suppose, for contradiction, that \(e_C\rightsquigarrow e_D\) for some \(e_D\notin E_B\cup E_B^+\). By (P3), choose \(v_i\in\operatorname{React}(e_C)\cap V_B\). Then
\begin{align}
e_B\rightsquigarrow v_i
& &&\text{by (P7)},\\
e_B\rightsquigarrow e_D
& &&\text{by transitivity (P6) applied to }e_B\rightsquigarrow v_i,\ v_i\in\operatorname{React}(e_C),\ e_C\rightsquigarrow e_D,\\
e_D\in E_B
& &&\text{by (P2)},
\end{align}
which contradicts \(e_D\notin E_B\cup E_B^+\). Hence no reaction outside \(\gamma_B\) is influenced by any \(e_C\in E_B^+\). For \(e_C\in E_B\), the same transitivity argument gives
\begin{align}
e_C\rightsquigarrow e_D\text{ and }e_D\notin E_B
&\Longrightarrow e_B\rightsquigarrow e_D &&\text{transitivity through }e_C,\\
&\Longrightarrow e_D\in E_B, &&\text{by (P2), contradiction.}
\end{align}
Therefore the influence of reactions in \(E_B\cup E_B^+\) is localized inside \(\gamma_B\).

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\gamma_B=(V_B,E_B\cup E_B^+)\text{ is output-complete and has localized influence}}
\]

\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_10:
\section*{Claim}
For the five-reaction network
\[
e_1:\varnothing\to v_1,
\quad e_2:v_1\to v_2,
\quad e_3:v_2\to v_3,
\quad e_4:v_3\to v_1,
\quad e_5:v_2\to\varnothing,
\]
with mass-action rates \(r_1=k_1\), \(r_2=k_2x_1\), \(r_3=k_3x_2\), \(r_4=k_4x_3\), \(r_5=k_5x_2\), the positive steady state is
\[
\bar x_1=\frac{k_1(k_3+k_5)}{k_2k_5},
\qquad
\bar x_2=\frac{k_1}{k_5},
\qquad
\bar x_3=\frac{k_1k_3}{k_4k_5}.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1)& \dot x_1=k_1-k_2x_1+k_4x_3.\\
(P2)& \dot x_2=k_2x_1-k_3x_2-k_5x_2.\\
(P3)& \dot x_3=k_3x_2-k_4x_3.\\
(P4)& \text{At steady state, }\dot x_1=\dot x_2=\dot x_3=0.\\
(P5)& k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4,k_5>0.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Use the third steady-state equation:
\begin{align}
0&=k_3\bar x_2-k_4\bar x_3 &&\text{by (P3) and (P4)}\\
\bar x_3&=\frac{k_3}{k_4}\bar x_2. &&\text{solve for }\bar x_3\text{ using }k_4>0
\end{align}
Use the first steady-state equation:
\begin{align}
0&=k_1-k_2\bar x_1+k_4\bar x_3 &&\text{by (P1) and (P4)}\\
k_2\bar x_1&=k_1+k_4\bar x_3 &&\text{rearrangement}\\
k_2\bar x_1&=k_1+k_3\bar x_2 &&\text{substitute }\bar x_3=\frac{k_3}{k_4}\bar x_2.
\end{align}
Use the second steady-state equation:
\begin{align}
0&=k_2\bar x_1-(k_3+k_5)\bar x_2 &&\text{by (P2) and (P4)}\\
(k_3+k_5)\bar x_2&=k_2\bar x_1 &&\text{rearrangement}\\
(k_3+k_5)\bar x_2&=k_1+k_3\bar x_2 &&\text{substitute previous expression for }k_2\bar x_1\\
k_5\bar x_2&=k_1 &&\text{subtract }k_3\bar x_2\\
\bar x_2&=\frac{k_1}{k_5}. &&\text{solve using }k_5>0
\end{align}
Then
\begin{align}
\bar x_3&=\frac{k_3}{k_4}\bar x_2=\frac{k_1k_3}{k_4k_5} &&\text{substitute }\bar x_2,\\
\bar x_1&=\frac{(k_3+k_5)\bar x_2}{k_2}=
\frac{k_1(k_3+k_5)}{k_2k_5}. &&\text{substitute }\bar x_2
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\bar x_1=\frac{k_1(k_3+k_5)}{k_2k_5},\qquad
\bar x_2=\frac{k_1}{k_5},\qquad
\bar x_3=\frac{k_1k_3}{k_4k_5}}
\]

\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_11:
\section*{Claim}
In the five-reaction mass-action example, perturbing \(k_3\) leaves \(\bar x_2\), \(\bar r_1\), and \(\bar r_5\) invariant, while the total concentration equation
\[
\frac{d}{dt}(x_1+x_2+x_3)=r_1-r_5
\]
acts as an integral-control identity imposing \(\bar x_2=k_1/k_5\) at steady state.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1)& \dot x_1=r_1-r_2+r_4.\\
(P2)& \dot x_2=r_2-r_3-r_5.\\
(P3)& \dot x_3=r_3-r_4.\\
(P4)& r_1=k_1,\quad r_5=k_5x_2.\\
(P5)& \bar x_2=k_1/k_5.\\
(P6)& \bar r_A=r_A(\bar x;k_A).\\
(P7)& \text{At steady state, }\dfrac{d}{dt}(x_1+x_2+x_3)=0.\\
(P8)& \text{A variable is invariant under }k_3\text{ if its derivative with respect to }k_3\text{ is }0.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Sum the rate equations:
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}(x_1+x_2+x_3)
&=\dot x_1+\dot x_2+\dot x_3 &&\text{linearity of }d/dt\\
&=(r_1-r_2+r_4)+(r_2-r_3-r_5)+(r_3-r_4) &&\text{by (P1)--(P3)}\\
&=r_1-r_5. &&\text{cancel }-r_2+r_2,\ -r_3+r_3,\ r_4-r_4
\end{align}
At steady state,
\begin{align}
0&=\bar r_1-\bar r_5 &&\text{by previous line and (P7)}\\
0&=k_1-k_5\bar x_2 &&\text{by (P4) and (P6)}\\
\bar x_2&=\frac{k_1}{k_5}. &&\text{solve for }\bar x_2
\end{align}
Differentiate the invariant quantities with respect to \(k_3\):
\begin{align}
\partial_{k_3}\bar x_2
&=\partial_{k_3}\left(\frac{k_1}{k_5}\right)=0 &&\text{by (P5)},\\
\bar r_1&=k_1 &&\text{by (P4)},\\
\partial_{k_3}\bar r_1&=0 &&\text{differentiate }k_1\text{ with respect to }k_3,\\
\bar r_5&=k_5\bar x_2=k_5\frac{k_1}{k_5}=k_1 &&\text{by (P4) and (P5)},\\
\partial_{k_3}\bar r_5&=0 &&\text{differentiate }k_1\text{ with respect to }k_3.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\frac{d}{dt}(x_1+x_2+x_3)=r_1-r_5\quad\text{and}\quad
\partial_{k_3}\bar x_2=\partial_{k_3}\bar r_1=\partial_{k_3}\bar r_5=0}
\]

\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_13:
\section*{Claim}
If \(c_{11}\in\ker S_{11}\) is decomposed into supported whole-network cycles and emergent cycles as
\[
c_{11}=\sum_\alpha w_\alpha c_1^{(\alpha)}+\sum_c w_c c^{(c)},
\qquad
u^{(c)}:=S_{21}c^{(c)},
\]
and \(P\) projects onto \(U^\perp\) for \(U:=\operatorname{span}\{\nu^{(c)}\}\), then the undetermined emergent-cycle coefficients \(w_c\) are eliminated by the projected integrator equation
\[
P Q\dot x=PS^\sharp r_2,
\qquad
Q:=\begin{pmatrix}-S_{21}S_{11}^+&I\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
S^\sharp:=S_{22}-S_{21}S_{11}^+S_{12}.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1)& \dfrac{d}{dt}(x_2-S_{21}S_{11}^+x_1)=S^\sharp r_2+S_{21}c_{11}.\\
(P2)& c_{11}=\sum_\alpha w_\alpha c_1^{(\alpha)}+\sum_c w_c c^{(c)}.\\
(P3)& c_1^{(\alpha)}\in(\ker S)_{\mathrm{supp}\,\gamma}\text{, hence }S_{21}c_1^{(\alpha)}=0.\\
(P4)& \nu^{(c)}:=S_{21}c^{(c)},\quad U:=\operatorname{span}\{\nu^{(c)}\}.\\
(P5)& P\text{ is the projection onto }U^\perp,\text{ so }P\nu^{(c)}=0\text{ for every }c.\\
(P6)& Q:=\begin{pmatrix}-S_{21}S_{11}^+&I\end{pmatrix},\quad x:=\begin{pmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{pmatrix}.\\
(P7)& Q\dot x=\dot x_2-S_{21}S_{11}^+\dot x_1.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Expand the unknown term in (P1):
\begin{align}
S_{21}c_{11}
&=S_{21}\left(\sum_\alpha w_\alpha c_1^{(\alpha)}+\sum_c w_c c^{(c)}\right) &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\sum_\alpha w_\alpha S_{21}c_1^{(\alpha)}+\sum_c w_cS_{21}c^{(c)} &&\text{linearity}\\
&=\sum_c w_c\nu^{(c)} &&\text{by (P3) and (P4)}.
\end{align}
Use (P1):
\begin{align}
\dot x_2-S_{21}S_{11}^+\dot x_1
&=S^\sharp r_2+\sum_c w_c\nu^{(c)} &&\text{by previous line and (P1)}.
\end{align}
Project onto \(U^\perp\):
\begin{align}
P(\dot x_2-S_{21}S_{11}^+\dot x_1)
&=PS^\sharp r_2+\sum_cw_cP\nu^{(c)} &&\text{apply }P\\
&=PS^\sharp r_2 &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
Use the definition of \(Q\):
\begin{align}
P Q\dot x
&=P(\dot x_2-S_{21}S_{11}^+\dot x_1) &&\text{by (P6) and (P7)}\\
&=PS^\sharp r_2. &&\text{previous result}
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{P Q\dot x=PS^\sharp r_2}
\]

\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_15:
\section*{Claim}
For the mass-action sniffer system
\[
\dot x_1=k_1x_3-k_2x_1x_2,
\qquad
\dot x_2=k_3x_3-k_4x_2,
\qquad
\dot x_3=k_5-k_6x_3,
\]
with positive parameters, the steady state satisfies
\[
\bar x_1=\frac{k_1k_4}{k_2k_3},
\qquad
\bar x_2=\frac{k_3k_5}{k_4k_6},
\qquad
\bar x_3=\frac{k_5}{k_6}.
\]
Consequently \(\bar x_1\) is independent of \(k_5\) and \(k_6\) under these mass-action equations.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1)& \dot x_1=k_1x_3-k_2x_1x_2.\\
(P2)& \dot x_2=k_3x_3-k_4x_2.\\
(P3)& \dot x_3=k_5-k_6x_3.\\
(P4)& \text{At steady state, }\dot x_1=\dot x_2=\dot x_3=0.\\
(P5)& k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4,k_5,k_6>0.\\
(P6)& \text{Independence from }k_j\text{ means }\partial_{k_j}\bar x_1=0.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Solve the third steady-state equation:
\begin{align}
0&=k_5-k_6\bar x_3 &&\text{by (P3) and (P4)}\\
\bar x_3&=\frac{k_5}{k_6}. &&\text{solve using }k_6>0
\end{align}
Solve the second steady-state equation:
\begin{align}
0&=k_3\bar x_3-k_4\bar x_2 &&\text{by (P2) and (P4)}\\
\bar x_2&=\frac{k_3}{k_4}\bar x_3 &&\text{solve using }k_4>0\\
&=\frac{k_3k_5}{k_4k_6}. &&\text{substitute }\bar x_3
\end{align}
Solve the first steady-state equation:
\begin{align}
0&=k_1\bar x_3-k_2\bar x_1\bar x_2 &&\text{by (P1) and (P4)}\\
k_2\bar x_1\bar x_2&=k_1\bar x_3 &&\text{rearrangement}\\
\bar x_1&=\frac{k_1\bar x_3}{k_2\bar x_2} &&\text{solve using }k_2>0\text{ and }\bar x_2>0\\
&=\frac{k_1(k_5/k_6)}{k_2(k_3k_5/(k_4k_6))} &&\text{substitute }\bar x_2\text{ and }\bar x_3\\
&=\frac{k_1k_4}{k_2k_3}. &&\text{cancel }k_5/k_6
\end{align}
Differentiate \(\bar x_1\) with respect to \(k_5\) and \(k_6\):
\begin{align}
\partial_{k_5}\bar x_1
&=\partial_{k_5}\left(\frac{k_1k_4}{k_2k_3}\right)=0 &&\text{no }k_5\text{ dependence},\\
\partial_{k_6}\bar x_1
&=\partial_{k_6}\left(\frac{k_1k_4}{k_2k_3}\right)=0 &&\text{no }k_6\text{ dependence}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\bar x_1=\frac{k_1k_4}{k_2k_3},\quad
\bar x_2=\frac{k_3k_5}{k_4k_6},\quad
\bar x_3=\frac{k_5}{k_6},\quad
\partial_{k_5}\bar x_1=\partial_{k_6}\bar x_1=0}
\]

\hfill$\blacksquare$
